title: L¹ contraction: ∫⁻‖k⋆g‖ₑ ≤ ∫⁻‖g‖ₑ for a nonnegative kernel with ∫k = 1
statement: Let n ∈ ℕ and ℝⁿ = Euclid n with Lebesgue measure. Let k : ℝⁿ → ℝ satisfy k(z) ≥ 0 for all z and ∫ k = 1 (Bochner integral). Let g : ℝⁿ → ℝ be a.e.-strongly measurable. Write (k ⋆ g)(x) := ∫ k(t) g(x − t) dt (Mathlib's convolution with lsmul ℝ ℝ and volume). Then ∫⁻ ‖(k ⋆ g)(x)‖ₑ dx ≤ ∫⁻ ‖g(x)‖ₑ dx, an inequality between [0, ∞]-valued Lebesgue integrals of extended norms. This is Young's inequality for a probability kernel.
lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (k g : Euclid n → ℝ), (∀ z, 0 ≤ k z) → ∫ z, k z = 1 → AEStronglyMeasurable g volume → ∫⁻ x, ‖convolution k g (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume x‖ₑ ≤ ∫⁻ x, ‖g x‖ₑ
